Direct-match (same-trait) candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254). Direct-match asthma candidates are present. The main limitation is endpoint mismatch risk versus generic asthma (pediatric-specific phenotype; covariates listed as Unknown), so its superiority for a generic asthma benchmark is not certain.

Runners-up: PGS001782 (PRS-CS-auto; ~884k variants) has a disease-focused global-biobank development context and reports both AUROC (0.659) and covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 (0.048844), providing PRS-comparable evidence consistent with the asthma heritability ceiling; however its evaluation is EUR-only and validation n is modest (7,128). All 6 candidates are direct EFO-mapped to atopic eczema, but endpoint fidelity differs materially. PGS002755 is the strongest bet for a hidden external benchmark because it targets an incident atopic dermatitis endpoint (phenotyping_reported: incident AD), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (1,090,702), and reports a PRS-associated effect size (HR high vs low PRS 1.249, EUR eval). This combination is structurally most consistent with better out-of-sample PRS performance than sparse GWAS-hit scores or therapy-specific paradoxical-eczema endpoints.

Runners-up: PGS004587 shares the same incident AD endpoint and covariate set as PGS002755 but is a 23-variant genome-wide-significant score with weaker reported HR (1.153), so it is plausibly next-best yet structurally less powerful. PGS001773 is disease-aligned but is restricted to moderate-to-severe AD and uses only 25 variants; its very high full-model AUROC/R² are likely covariate-driven/non-comparable (and R² exceeds the provided EUR h2_obs ceiling), reducing confidence despite multi-ancestry evaluation. Overall confidence is only Moderate because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only AUROC/R², and several are endpoint-mismatched to generic eczema risk (paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis).
